title: Consumer complaints: filter then rank by urgency
prompt: Find complaints about charges continuing after cancellation or unauthorized recurring charges, then rank by urgency.
notes: The full 5,000-row demo sample (8 of the 15 columns) so the one-shot request stays under the 272K-token long-context tier; the 100,000-row file used in the walkthrough is ~6,783,860 tokens and cannot be sent to gpt-6-astra in one request at all.

The 2026 CFPB export has no free-text narratives; both approaches judge the Product / Issue / Sub-issue text, so matches are rare. There is no gold label; 169 rows carry a topical keyword (unauthorized / cancel / recurring / continuing / can't stop withdrawals) and the share of selected rows carrying one is reported only as a sanity check.

questions.name: ongoing_charges
questions.instruction: Does this complaint concern either charges continuing after cancellation or unauthorized recurring charges? The text may be in any language; judge its meaning using only the supplied product and issue fields.

criteria.true: The fields explicitly state or clearly imply that billing, charges, or debits continue after cancellation of a service, subscription, account, or payment authorization; OR they describe recurring charges that the consumer did not authorize. Implied statements count: being billed despite ending a subscription or revoking automatic-payment permission qualifies without the exact words 'after cancellation'. Unauthorized subscription billing or repeating automatic debits qualifies when the recurring nature is clear.
criteria.false: The complaint concerns a different issue, an isolated unauthorized transaction, an authorized recurring charge disputed only for its amount or fees, or cancellation without continued billing. A generic unauthorized-transaction, withdrawal, or purchase-dispute label alone does not establish recurring charges. If the fields leave the required recurrence or post-cancellation connection unresolved, treat the evidence as uncertain rather than inventing that connection.

questions.name: urgency
questions.instruction: Rate how urgently this complaint needs intervention based only on harm and immediacy supported by the supplied fields. The text may be in any language; judge its meaning. Do not infer financial hardship, imminent deadlines, or compromised accounts merely from the product or issue type. Use the highest supported level; absent specific urgency signals, use the lowest level, which means limited evidence rather than proven absence of risk.
levels: Limited urgency evidence: The fields identify the charge dispute but do not establish active financial harm, immediate consequences, or a pressing need to intervene.
Ongoing financial harm: The fields indicate active continuing debits, repeated unauthorized billing, or unsuccessful attempts to stop charges, without evidence of severe consequences.
Serious financial consequences: The fields indicate overdraft, mounting penalties, loss of access to funds, or difficulty paying essential expenses caused by the charges.

Critical immediate harm: The fields explicitly indicate an immediate threat to basic needs, such as inability to obtain food, medicine, or housing, or an active account compromise draining essential funds.

plan.title: Ongoing charges ranked by urgency
